316710.title: Real-rootedness and positivity conjecture for checkerboard triangulation polynomials
316710.literal:
For each $n\geq 0$, let $w_n(t)$ be the colour-imbalance generating Laurent polynomial for checkerboard triangulations of the marked polygon $P_n$, and define the homogeneous polynomial

$$
Q_n(u,v)=\sqrt{uv}^{\,n}\,w_n\left(\sqrt{\frac{u}{v}}\right)\in\mathbb N[u,v].
$$

The coefficient of $u^\alpha v^\beta$ counts checkerboard triangulations involving $\alpha$ black and $\beta$ white triangles.

**Real-rootedness and positivity conjecture.** (i) The polynomials $Q_0(u,1),Q_1(u,1),\dots\in\mathbb N[u]$ have only real roots, all of which are non-positive, and the non-zero roots of $Q_n(u,1)$ interleave the non-zero roots of $Q_{n+3}(u,1)$. (ii) The symmetric polynomial $Q_n(u,v)+Q_n(v,u)$ is of the form $R_n(u+v,uv)$, where $R_n(e_1,e_2)\in\mathbb Z[e_1,e_2]$ involves only positive coefficients.

These are experimental conjectural properties concerning the root geometry and coefficient positivity of the triangulation polynomials. The source gives no proof or resolution for either assertion.

317838.title: The enhanced conflict graph extreme-point conjecture for 2×N switches
317838.literal: Consider a $2\times N$ switch with traffic consisting of unicasts and broadcasts, and let $G$ be its enhanced conflict graph. Let $QSTAB(G)$ denote the fractional stable set polytope, and let $STAB(G)$ denote the stable set polytope. The stable sets of $G$ and the points $\boldsymbol{v}(m,U,V)$ described in Theorem 2 are known extreme points of $QSTAB(G)$. **The enhanced conflict graph extreme-point conjecture.** $QSTAB(G)$ has no other extreme points besides the stable sets and the points $\boldsymbol{v}(m,U,V)$. If true, the stated bound on the fractional weighted chromatic number would imply that an expansion factor of $1.25$ suffices for every vertex of $QSTAB(G)$ in the $2\times N$ case. This remains a conjecture in the paper; simulations motivate extending the approach to $K\times N$ switches.

319187.title: A lower bound for the ratio of the polynomials R_d and P_d
319187.literal:

$$

$$

This conjecture is presented as information needed to make the paper's expression for the focal function $g(s_1,s_2)$ useful; the source provides no resolution evidence.

319970.title: Pattern-avoidance formulation of the Riemann Hypothesis
319970.literal:
Let $\widetilde{{\mathfrak A}}_{n}\left(\substack{\displaystyle{\niv{\scriptstyle 1{\kern 1.75pt}2}{\kern 1.75pt}{\scriptstyle 3}} \\ \displaystyle{\vinb{\scriptstyle 2{\kern 1.75pt}1{\kern 1.75pt}3}}}\right)$ be the set of permutations in the relevant pattern-avoidance equivalence classes, and for $\delta$ in this set let the location of $1$ in $\delta$ denote its position. **Equivalent to RH.** The inequality

$$
\sum_{\delta \in \widetilde{{\mathfrak A}}_{n}\left(\substack{\displaystyle{\niv{\scriptstyle 1{\kern 1.75pt}2}{\kern 1.75pt}{\scriptstyle 3}} \\ \displaystyle{\vinb{\scriptstyle 2{\kern 1.75pt}1{\kern 1.75pt}3}}}\right)} (\textrm{location of $1$ in $\delta$}) < e^\gamma \log \log n
$$

holds for all $n \geq 5041$. By Robin's theorem, this is a reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis through the sum-of-divisors function, since the displayed sum equals $\sigma(n)$.

321135.title: Maximality conjecture for triples of consecutive patterns
321135.literal:
Let $S_k$ denote the set of permutations of length $k$, let $\binom{S_k}{3}$ denote its three-element subsets, and let $\alpha_B(n)$ be the number of permutations of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $B$. For a fixed pattern length $k$, define

$$
B=\{1 2 \ldots k,2 3 \ldots k 1,k 1 2 \ldots (k-1)\}.
$$

**Maximality conjecture for triples.** The pattern set $B$ is the maximal pattern set among sets of three patterns, in the sense that

$$
\alpha_B(n)\geq\alpha_{B'}(n)
$$

for all $B'\in\binom{S_k}{3}$ and all $n$. This conjecture is based on empirical evidence in the source, which gives no resolution.

321467.title: Surjective homomorphism swapping conjecture for simple graphs
321467.literal:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. For graphs $A$ and $B$, let $\operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{surj}}(A,B)$ be the set of graph homomorphisms whose vertex maps are surjective, and write $\hom^{\mathrm{surj}}(A,B)=|\operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{surj}}(A,B)|$.

**Surjective homomorphism swapping conjecture.** For every positive integer $i$,

$$
\hom^{\mathrm{surj}}(G\sqcup G,K_i)\leq \hom^{\mathrm{surj}}(G\times K_2,K_i).
$$

This is presented as a coefficientwise strengthening of the comparison between $P(G\sqcup G,q)$ and $P(G\times K_2,q)$, and the source notes that it would imply the conjecture that $K_q$ is strongly GT. The resolution status is not specified.

331982.title: Kernel–diadem inequality for graphs
331982.literal:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. Write $\ker(G)$ for its kernel, $\diadem(G)$ for its diadem, and $\alpha(G)$ for its independence number. **Kernel–diadem conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\left\lvert \mathrm{ker}(G)\right\rvert+\left\lvert \mathrm{diadem}(G)\right\rvert\leq 2\alpha(G).
$$

This is a universal inequality concerning two families of critical independent-set vertices. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence for this claim, so its status remains open.

343095.title: Fomin–Zelevinsky's exchange-graph conjecture for cluster patterns
343095.literal: Let $\mathbf{\Sigma}=\{\Sigma_t=(\mathbf{x}_t,\mathbf{y}_t,B_t)\mid t\in\mathbb{T}_n\}$ be a cluster pattern with coefficients in any semifield $\mathbb{P}$. An unlabeled cluster is the set $\{x_{1;t},\dots,x_{n;t}\}$, and an unlabeled seed is the equivalence class of labeled seeds obtained by permutations. Let the exchange graph be the quotient graph of $\mathbb{T}_n$ by equality of unlabeled seeds. **Fomin–Zelevinsky's exchange-graph conjecture.** The following properties hold: (a) each unlabeled cluster uniquely determines an unlabeled seed containing it; (b) the exchange graph depends only on the $B$-pattern $\mathbf{B}$; and (c) two unlabeled clusters are adjacent if and only if they have exactly $n-1$ common $x$-variables. The conjecture is stated as true in the source: all three claims were proved, with full generality attributed to Cao (2018), and claim (c) also follows from (a).

375419.title: Hamiltonian path pattern conjecture for labelled graph notations
375419.literal:
Let $G$ be a graph with labelled linear notation $I[G]$, where the colouring algorithm assigns natural-number colours $1,2,\ldots,n$ to the vertices and adjacent numbers must be connected by an edge. A Hamiltonian path is a path that passes through every vertex exactly once. The notation $\#\ \#\ \#$ denotes a string of return codes with abstract edges $\rightarrow \#1\ldots\rightarrow \#m$.

**Hamiltonian path pattern conjecture.** In order for a Hamiltonian path to exist on $I[G]$, it is necessary and sufficient that $I[G]$ satisfy one of the four possible patterns:

$$
I[G] = 1 \Big[_{1} \rightarrow k \Big[_{2} \ldots \Big] \, \Big]
$$

$$
I[G] = 1 \Big[_{1} \rightarrow k_{1} \Big[_{2} \ldots \Big]; \rightarrow k_{2} \Big[_{2} \ldots \Big] \, \Big]
$$

$$
I[G] = 1 \Big[_{1}... \rightarrow k_{1} \Big[_{i1} \#\#\#; \rightarrow k_{2} \Big[_{i2} \rightarrow \#1... \Big] \, \Big]; \rightarrow k_{3} \Big[_{i3} \ldots \Big] \, \Big]
$$

$$
I[G] = 1 \Big[_{1}... \rightarrow k_{1} \Big[_{i1} \#\#\#; \rightarrow k_{2} \Big[_{i2}... \rightarrow k_{3} \Big[_{i3} \rightarrow \#1; \, \#\#\# \Big] \, \Big] \, \Big]; \rightarrow k_{4} \Big[_{i4} \ldots \Big] \, \Big]
$$

Inside the blocks $\Big[_{2}\ldots \Big]$, $\Big[_{i2}\ldots \Big]$, $\Big[_{i3}\ldots \Big]$ and $\Big[_{i4}\ldots \Big]$, the number of nested brackets must be exactly equal to the number of abstract vertices, with no extra branching allowed. This conjecture was put forward based on an enumeration of graphs with at most seven vertices; its validity beyond that tested range remains open.

376588.title: The spanning-tree factorization conjecture for Sierpinski gaskets
376588.literal:
Let $SG_d(n)$ be the $d$-dimensional Sierpinski gasket at stage $n$, and let $f_d(n)=N_{ST}(SG_d(n))$ denote its number of spanning trees. Define exponents $\alpha_d(n)$, $\beta_d(n)$, and $\gamma_d(n)$ by

$$
\alpha_d(n)=\frac{d-1}{2}\bigl[(d+1)^n-1\bigr],
$$

$$
\beta_d(n)=\frac{d-1}{2d}\bigl[(d+1)^{n+1}+dn+d-1\bigr],
$$

$$
\gamma_d(n)=\frac{d-1}{2d}\bigl[(d+1)^n-dn-1\bigr].
$$

**Spanning-tree factorization conjecture.** The number of spanning trees is

$$
f_d(n)=2^{\alpha_d(n)}(d+1)^{\beta_d(n)}(d+3)^{\gamma_d(n)}.
$$

This conjecture extends the simple prime-factor formulas established for the two-, three-, and four-dimensional Sierpinski gaskets. The stated exponents are positive integers for positive integer $d$ and non-negative integer $n$, and the formula agrees at $n=0$ with the spanning-tree count $(d+1)^{d-1}$ for the complete graph $SG_d(0)$. A general proof or explanatory method for the unexpectedly simple solution is not supplied.

376948.title: Ridge-graph structure conjecture for NHM m-hemimetric cones
376948.literal:
Let $NHM_n^m$ be the cone of nonnegative $m$-hemimetrics. Denote by $T_{i_1\dots i_{m+1},i_{m+2}}$ an $(m+1)$-simplex facet and by $N_{i_1\dots i_{m+1}}$ a nonnegativity facet. Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the two facet orbits, and write $G(F_2)$ for the subgraph induced by $F_2$. **Ridge-graph structure conjecture.** The ridge graph of $NHM_n^m$ satisfies: (i) $T_{i_1\dots i_{m+1},i_{m+2}}$ is adjacent to every other facet except the following $m+2$ facets: all other $(m+1)$-simplex facets with the same support and $N_{i_1\dots i_{m+1}}$; (ii)

$$
G(F_2)=\overline{J(n,3)}\quad\text{for }m=2,
$$

and

$$
G(F_2)=K_{\binom{n}{m+1}}\quad\text{for }m\geq 3.
$$

Consequently, the restriction to $F_1$ is $G(F_1)=K_{m+2,\dots,m+2}$, and the conjecture would imply that the ridge graph of $NHM_n^m$ has diameter $2$. The diameter-$2$ conclusion is known for $m=1$, where $NHM_n^1=MET_n$.

376959.title: Spectral approximation conjecture for Harper operators on amenable graphs
376959.literal:
Let $X$ be a graph with a free action by an amenable group $amma]$, with finite fundamental domain. Let $\{X_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ be the regular exhaustion of $X$ corresponding to a regular exhaustion $\Lambda_m$ of $\Gamma$. For each $m$, let $N_m$ be the size of $\Lambda_m$, and let $E_m(\lambda)$ denote the number of eigenvalues less than or equal to $\lambda$ of the DML restricted to $X_m$, with either Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions. Let $F$ be the spectral density function of the DML on $X$, defined using the von Neumann trace.

**Spectral approximation conjecture.** The normalized eigenvalue-counting functions converge to the spectral density function:

$$
\lim_{m\rightarrow\infty}\frac{E_m(\lambda)}{N_m}=F(\lambda),\qquad\forall\lambda\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

This conjecture asserts that finite-volume restrictions of the DML recover the spectral density of the infinite graph, independently of whether Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions are used. Its status is not determined by the supplied text.

378558.title: Hatayama's structural conjecture for the crystal B^{2,s} of type D_n^{(1)}
378558.literal:
Let $B^{2,s}$ be a crystal of type $D_n^{(1)}$, and let $B(k\varpi_2)$ denote the classical crystal of highest weight $k\varpi_2$. Let $D_{B^{2,s}}$ be an energy function on $B^{2,s}$. **Hatayama's structural conjecture.** If the crystal $B^{2,s}$ exists, then, as a classical crystal, it satisfies

$$
B^{2,s}\cong\bigoplus_{k=0}^{s}B(k\varpi_2),
$$

it is perfect of level $s$, and its energy function satisfies $D_{B^{2,s}}(b)=k-s$ whenever $b$ belongs to the component $B(k\varpi_2)$. These properties are the specific type $D_n^{(1)}$, node $2$ case of the conjectural structure of Kirillov–Reshetikhin crystals. The paper constructs a combinatorial model and proves uniqueness under the assumed existence and stated properties, but the existence of the affine crystal itself remains open in the source.

378669.title: Shareshian–Wachs conjecture for the matching complex homology representation
378669.literal:
Let $n=2k$ be even. The complexes ${\mathsf {NPM}}_n$ and the poset ${\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}$ have reduced homology groups carrying actions of $S_n$, where $\varepsilon_n$ denotes the sign character of $S_n$. The poset ${\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}$ consists of trees with $n$ bijectively labelled leaves whose nonleaves have degree congruent to $2$ modulo $2$ but are not of degree $2$, and its order-complex homology is concentrated in dimension $t$. **Shareshian–Wachs conjecture.** There is an isomorphism of $S_n$-modules

$$
\widetilde{H}_{3k-4}({\mathsf {NPM}}_n) \cong_{S_n} \widetilde{H}_t(\Delta {\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}) \otimes \varepsilon_n.
$$

This strengthens the stated Shareshian–Wachs theorem, which identifies the restriction of the left-hand side to $S_{n-1}$ with the corresponding homology representation. The conjecture concerns the full $S_n$-module structure and is unresolved in the supplied source.

378939.title: Hollmann's pseudocyclicity conjecture for the Frobenius fusion scheme
378939.literal:
Let $q=2^m$, let ${\cal E}$ be the set of exterior lines to a fixed nonsingular conic in ${\rm PG}(2,q)$, and let $({\cal E},\{\Gamma_a\})$ be the elliptic association scheme. For $a\in {\bf T}_0^*$, define the Frobenius orbit

$$
C_a=\{a,a^2,a^4,\ldots,a^{2^{m-1}}\}
$$

and set

$$
\Delta_a=\bigcup_{i\in C_a}\Gamma_i.
$$

Let ${\cal R}$ be a set of representatives for the Frobenius orbits on ${\bf T}_0^*$. The fusion scheme $({\cal E},\{\Delta_a\})$ is obtained by merging the classes of the elliptic scheme along these orbits.

**Hollmann's conjecture.** If $m$ is an odd prime, then $({\cal E},\{\Delta_a\})$ is pseudocyclic.

When $m$ is prime, each nontrivial Frobenius orbit has size $m$, so the fusion scheme has equal nontrivial valencies. The conjecture asserts the remaining condition needed for pseudocyclicity; the source gives no resolution.

378962.title: Freiman's structural conjecture for sets with doubling near three times their size
378962.literal:
Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers, write $|A|=k$, and let $2A=A+A=\{a+a':a,a'\in A\}$. An **arithmetic progression** is a finite set of equally spaced integers, and a **bi-progression** is the corresponding structured object used in Freiman's theorem.

**Freiman's conjecture.** There exists a natural number $K$ such that for any finite set of natural numbers $A$ with $|A|=k>K$ and

$$
|2A|=3k-3+b,\qquad 0\leqslant b<\frac{1}{3}k-2,
$$

$A$ is either a subset of an arithmetic progression of length at most $2k-1+2b$ or a subset of a bi-progression of length at most $k+b$.

This conjecture seeks a precise structural description of large finite sets whose sumset has size just above three times the size of the original set. The surrounding discussion records earlier partial results of Freiman and indicates that the conjecture was unresolved in the source.

379222.title: Tautness conjecture for pseudo primitive idempotents
379222.literal: Let $\Gamma$ be a bipartite distance-regular graph, and let $T$ denote its subconstituent algebra. Assume that, up to isomorphism, there exist exactly two irreducible $T$-modules with endpoint $2$, and that both are thin. Choose $\xi,\chi\in\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ such that $\widetilde{\xi}$ and $\widetilde{\chi}$ are the local eigenvalues of these modules. Let $E$ and $F$ be pseudo primitive idempotents of $\Gamma$ for $\xi$ and $\chi$, respectively. **Tautness conjecture.** The pair $E,F$ is taut, meaning that $E\circ F$ is a linear combination of at most two pseudo primitive idempotents of $\Gamma$. This conjecture predicts a connection between the thin endpoint-$2$ modules of the subconstituent algebra and taut pairs of pseudo primitive idempotents; its resolution is not specified in the source.

379294.title: The cover-to-domination cover pebbling ratio conjecture
379294.literal:
Let $G$ be a graph with more than one vertex. Write $\lambda(G)$ for its cover pebbling number and $\psi(G)$ for its domination cover pebbling number. **Cover-to-domination cover pebbling ratio conjecture.** The ratio $lambda(G)/psi(G)$ should satisfy

$$
\frac{\lambda(G)}{\psi(G)}\geq 3.
$$

The paper notes that this bound is attained by the complete graph on two vertices and that graph families can make the ratio arbitrarily close to $3$ from above; whether the bound holds for every graph remains open.

379786.title: Mills–Robbins–Rumsey's refined vertical-symmetry conjecture
379786.literal:
Let $n\geq1$, let $1\leq r\leq2n-1$, let $\TSPP{2n+1}$ be the triangular shifted plane partitions defined above, and let $\gamma$ be the odd-diagonal flip involution. Write $U_2(b)$ for the statistic defined above, let $\TSPP{2n+1}^{\gamma}$ be the set of $\gamma$-invariant elements, and let $A_{2n+1}^{\mathrm{VS}}(t)$ denote the refined enumerator of vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices.

**Mills–Robbins–Rumsey's refined vertical-symmetry conjecture.** The number of $b\in\TSPP{2n+1}$ satisfying $\gamma(b)=b$ and $U_2(b)=r-1$ should equal the number of vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices satisfying the stated first-column condition $a_{i1}=1$; equivalently,

$$
\sum_{b\in\TSPP{2n+1}^{\gamma}}t^{U_2(b)}=A_{2n+1}^{\mathrm{VS}}(t).
$$

The conjecture gives a refined enumeration for the vertical-symmetry class. The paper proves a determinant formula for the left-hand generating function, but the claimed equality with the alternating-sign-matrix polynomial is presented as conjectural.
